title: kv-cache: improve eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation and enable safe spillover paging
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncontrolled spillover have been a recurring source of OOMs and tail latency spikes on long-context workloads. This PR implements a set of eviction and memory-management changes designed to reduce fragmentation, enable bounded spillover (paging) to local SSD, and perform background compaction to maintain usable contiguous regions for large KV entries. Key changes: 1) Segment-aware eviction policy that prefers evicting small/fragmented segments and those with low reuse score instead of pure LRU; 2) Background defragmentation/compaction worker that runs opportunistically under low-load windows to merge adjacent free segments; 3) Bounded spillover paging to local NVMe with an IO rate limiter and prioritization rules (evict-first vs spill-first configurable per deployment); 4) Eviction priority tiers and a metadata-level heap that avoids scanning entire cache for candidate segments; 5) New metrics and tracing hooks (kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv.cache.spill_io_ops, kv.cache.evictions_by_cause, kv.cache.compaction_ops) and runtime flags to tune thresholds. Backwards compatibility and rollout: all spillover and compaction behaviors are disabled by default for existing clusters; new flags are gated behind feature flags and enterprise config for Dedicated/Private. There is a safe fallback path that reverts to previous LRU behavior if the spill subsystem is unhealthy. Performance: on perf-canary with long-context (32k) workloads we observed 30-40% reduction in fragmentation_ratio, 35% average memory reclaimed before OOM, and p99 latency improved 8-12% for heavy KV workloads; incidents caused by OOMs dropped ~90% in canary. Testing: unit tests cover new eviction heuristics and spill path, integration tests validate spill IO rate limiting under synthetic load, and perf-canary runs validate real workload behavior. Migration notes: operators should enable spillover on low-traffic windows, monitor new metrics, and start with conservative spill thresholds (spill_threshold=0.92, compaction_target=0.6). See docs/operational/kv-cache.md for operations steps. Checklist: - [x] Implement segment-aware eviction - [x] Implement compaction worker - [x] Implement bounded spill/paging with rate limiter - [x] Add metrics and tracing - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Perf-canary validation - [x] Docs and rollout notes Commits below are squashed for merge; see commit history for details.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you explain how the segment heap avoids full-cache scans? Concerned about CPU overhead under high QPS.

Avery Chen: The heap stores candidate segment heads and is updated on small mutations only; we avoid full scans by updating heuristics incrementally and capping rescans to background compaction windows. Measured CPU impact is <2% in perf-canary.
Priya Natarajan: How do we ensure spill IO doesn't impact inference latency? Need a clear IO throttling strategy and observability.

Avery Chen: Added a token-bucket rate limiter for spill IO, plus a latency-priority queue that suspends non-critical spill jobs when tail latency crosses SLO thresholds. Exposed metrics kv.cache.spill_io_ops and kv.cache.spill_backpressure to alert on regressions.
Liam O'Connor: Request minor API rename for clarity (Segment -> SegmentHandle). Also please add a comment describing compaction invariants.
Avery Chen: Renamed Segment -> SegmentHandle and added invariants and delta tests. PTAL.
Miguel Santos: CI had a flake in integration tests; tests are flaky on slower builders. Please add retry in test harness.
Avery Chen: Increased integration test timeouts and added a hermetic retry for the perf stage. Reran CI.
Liam O'Connor: LGTM after CI green and perf-canary results look stable.
